title: Korea Post says hackers using overseas IPs took customer data via Internet Post Office
date_note: Newsis (published 27 November) is the page read; it says the breach was noticed on 25 November and gives no earlier public statement.
geo_basis: country: Newsis names Korea Post and the Ministry of Science and ICT; no city stated
summary: Newsis reports that the Postal Service Bureau and the Ministry of Science and ICT confirmed customer data was leaked in an external hacking attack from overseas IP addresses. Names, addresses and phone numbers of customers with mail in transit were looked up through the mobile Internet Post Office's delivery location change service. Newsis's headline gives the damage for the one day analysed so far as 11만3855명 (people, including corporations); the total scale is under investigation.
plain: Korea Post confirmed, per Newsis, that hackers using overseas IP addresses obtained names, addresses and phone numbers of customers; the one day analysed so far covers 11만3855명, and the total is under investigation.
exec: Newsis reports a confirmed customer-data leak, with the day analysed so far covering 11만3855명; the total is still under investigation.
action: As Newsis reports the authorities' advice: be wary of suspicious texts or calls impersonating the post office that ask to change an address or pay extra delivery fees.

validation.note: Only Newsis was read; it relays statements by the Postal Service Bureau and the Ministry of Science and ICT. The ministry's or Korea Post's own release was not read.
